Azure VMs Deep: Azure Virtual Machines are IaaS compute. VM series: General purpose (B-series burstable, D-series balanced), Compute optimized (F-series), Memory optimized (E-series, M-series), Storage optimized (L-series), GPU (NC, ND, NV). Availability Sets distribute VMs across fault/update domains (99.95% SLA). Availability Zones provide 99.99% SLA. Azure Dedicated Host for compliance. VM Scale Sets automatically manage identical VMs with autoscaling. Proximity Placement Groups reduce inter-VM latency.

# Create VM
az vm create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --name my-vm \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size Standard_B2s \
  --admin-username azureuser \
  --generate-ssh-keys \
  --availability-zone 1 \
  --public-ip-sku Standard

# Resize VM
az vm resize --resource-group my-rg --name my-vm --size Standard_D4s_v5

# Deallocate (stops billing)
az vm deallocate --resource-group my-rg --name my-vm

# VM Scale Set
az vmss create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --name web-vmss \
  --instance-count 3 \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size Standard_B2s \
  --upgrade-policy-mode automatic

# Autoscale rule
az monitor autoscale create --resource web-vmss --resource-group my-rg --resource-type Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets \
  --condition "Percentage CPU > 75 avg 5m" --scale-out 2
  --condition "Percentage CPU < 30 avg 5m" --scale-in 1
Azure App Service: App Service is PaaS for web apps, REST APIs, and mobile backends. Supports .NET, Java, Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Docker containers. Plans define pricing tier: Free/Shared (dev), Basic (custom domain, manual scale), Standard (auto-scale, staging slots), Premium (private endpoints, increased scale). Deployment Slots enable staging (swap with zero downtime). Auto-scale based on metrics or schedule. Built-in authentication (Entra ID, Google, Facebook). Hybrid Connections connect to on-prem resources. App Service Environment (ASE) is fully isolated, dedicated.

# Create App Service plan
az appservice plan create \
  --name my-plan \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --sku S1 \
  --is-linux

# Create web app
az webapp create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --plan my-plan \
  --name my-app \
  --runtime "NODE:20-lts"

# Deploy from GitHub
az webapp deployment source config \
  --name my-app \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --repo-url https://github.com/user/my-app \
  --branch main

# Create staging slot
az webapp deployment slot create \
  --name my-app \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --slot staging

# Swap slots
az webapp deployment slot swap \
  --name my-app \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --slot staging --target-slot production
Azure Functions: Azure Functions is serverless compute. Triggers: HTTP (API), Timer, Blob Storage, Queue Storage, Event Grid, Cosmos DB, Service Bus. Hosting plans: Consumption (pay per execution, auto-scale to zero), Premium (pre-warmed instances, VNet integration, unlimited execution), Dedicated (on App Service plan). Durable Functions for stateful workflows (function chaining, fan-out/fan-in, human interaction). Supports C#, JavaScript, Python, Java, PowerShell, TypeScript. Managed dependencies with PowerShell.

# Create Function App
az functionapp create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --consumption-plan-location eastus \
  --runtime python \
  --runtime-version 3.11 \
  --functions-version 4 \
  --name my-func \
  --storage-account mystorage

# Python HTTP trigger
# import azure.functions as func
# def main(req: func.HttpRequest) -> func.HttpResponse:
#     name = req.params.get('name')
#     return func.HttpResponse(f"Hello {name}!")

# Deploy
func azure functionapp publish my-func

# [FunctionName("ProcessOrder")]
# public async Task ProcessOrder(
#     [OrchestrationTrigger] IDurableOrchestrationContext ctx)
# {
#     var order = ctx.GetInput<Order>();
#     await ctx.CallActivityAsync("ValidatePayment", order);
#     await ctx.CallActivityAsync("UpdateInventory", order);
#     await ctx.CallActivityAsync("SendConfirmation", order);

Azure Container Apps & AKS: Azure Container Apps (ACA): serverless containers, auto-scaling (including scale to zero), HTTP ingress, revisions, Dapr integration, KEDA scaling. Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): managed Kubernetes, automated upgrades, node pools, Azure AD integration, Azure Policy for Gatekeeper, advanced networking (Calico/Cilium). Azure Container Instances (ACI): simple single-pod containers, fast startup, no orchestration. Azure Container Registry (ACR): private Docker registry, geo-replication, task automation.

# Create Container App
az containerapp create \
  --name my-app \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --environment my-env \
  --image nginx:alpine \
  --target-port 80 \
  --ingress external

# Create AKS cluster
az aks create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --name my-aks \
  --node-count 3 \
  --enable-cluster-autoscaler \
  --min-count 1 --max-count 10 \
  --enable-oidc-issuer \
  --enable-workload-identity

# Get credentials
az aks get-credentials --resource-group my-rg --name my-aks

# ACR
az acr create --resource-group my-rg --name myregistry --sku Basic
az acr build --registry myregistry --image web-app:v1 .
Azure Batch & HPC: Azure Batch runs large-scale parallel and HPC workloads. Creates and manages a pool of VMs, installs applications, schedules tasks. Auto-scale pool size based on queue depth. Low-priority VMs for up to 80% cost savings (can be preempted). Integration with Azure Storage for input/output. Azure CycleCloud for HPC cluster management. Useful for rendering, financial modeling, genomics, and Monte Carlo simulations.

# Create Batch account
az batch account create \
  --name my-batch \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus

# Create pool
az batch pool create \
  --account-name my-batch \
  --id my-pool \
  --vm-size Standard_D2s_v3 \
  --target-dedicated-nodes 10 \
  --image canonical:ubuntuserver:22_04-lts-gen2:latest \
  --node-agent-sku-id batch.node.ubuntu 22.04

# Submit job
az batch job create --account-name my-batch --id my-job --pool-id my-pool

# Submit task
az batch task create --account-name my-batch --job-id my-job --task-id task1 --command-line "echo Hello"

Azure Blob Storage: Azure Blob Storage is object storage for unstructured data. Access tiers: Hot (frequent, lowest access cost), Cool (infrequent, 30-day min), Cold (rare, 90-day min), Archive (offline, 180-day min, hours to retrieve). Storage types: Block blobs (general objects, up to 4.7TB), Append blobs (logs), Page blobs (VHDs, up to 8TB). Lifecycle management auto-tiers data. Immutable storage (WORM) for compliance. Soft delete protects against accidental deletion. Azure Files is managed SMB/NFS file shares. Static websites can be hosted directly from blob storage.

# Create storage account
az storage account create \
  --name mystorageaccount \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_GRS \
  --kind StorageV2 \
  --min-tls-version TLS1_2

# Upload blob
az storage blob upload \
  --account-name mystorageaccount \
  --container-name data \
  --name myfile.txt \
  --file ./myfile.txt

# Generate SAS token
az storage blob generate-sas \
  --account-name mystorageaccount \
  --container-name data \
  --name myfile.txt \
  --permissions r \
  --expiry 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z

# Lifecycle policy (via JSON)
az storage account management-policy create \
  --account-name mystorageaccount \
  --policy @policy.json
# policy.json: tier to Cool after 30d, Archive after 90d, delete after 365d
Azure Disk Storage: Azure Managed Disks are block storage for VMs. Types: Ultra Disk (sub-ms latency, provisioned IOPS), Premium SSD v2 (high performance, cost-optimized), Premium SSD (production workloads), Standard SSD (dev/test), Standard HDD (backup, non-critical). Disk roles: OS disk (up to 4TB), data disks (up to 32TB per disk). Encryption at rest: SSE (platform-managed) or customer-managed keys (Azure Key Vault). Azure Disk Encryption via BitLocker (Windows) or DM-Crypt (Linux). Shared disks (Windows Server Failover Cluster, Linux Pacemaker). Incremental snapshots for backup.

# Create managed disk
az disk create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --name data-disk \
  --size-gb 256 \
  --sku PremiumSSD_LRS \
  --zone 1

# Attach to VM
az vm disk attach \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --vm-name my-vm \
  --name data-disk

# Create snapshot
az snapshot create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --name data-snapshot \
  --source data-disk

# Create disk from snapshot
az disk create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --name data-disk-restored \
  --source data-snapshot

# Resize disk
az disk update --resource-group my-rg --name data-disk --size-gb 512
Azure Files & NetApp Files: Azure Files provides fully managed SMB and NFS file shares. Accessible from Windows, Linux, macOS via standard file protocols. SMB Multichannel for performance. Azure File Sync caches shares on Windows Servers (hybrid). Identity-based auth (Entra ID DS or AD DS). Azure NetApp Files (ANF): enterprise-grade, high-performance NFS/SMB, on bare metal, sub-ms latency, up to 100GB/s throughput. Multiple service levels: Standard, Premium, Ultra. Cross-region replication for DR.

# Create file share
az storage share create \
  --account-name mystorageaccount \
  --name myshare \
  --quota 100

# Mount on Linux
sudo mount -t cifs //mystorageaccount.file.core.windows.net/myshare /mnt/files \
  -o vers=3.0,username=mystorageaccount,password=xxx,dir_mode=0777,file_mode=0777

# Create NetApp account and volume
az netappfiles account create --resource-group my-rg --name my-netapp --location eastus
az netappfiles pool create --resource-group my-rg --account-name my-netapp --name my-pool --size 4 --service-level Premium
az netappfiles volume create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --account-name my-netapp \
  --pool-name my-pool \
  --name my-volume \
  --file-path my-unique-path \
  --usage-threshold 100 \
  --subnet /subscriptions/.../subnets/default \
  --protocol-types NFSv3
Azure CDN & Front Door: Azure CDN is a global CDN with point-of-presence (POP) locations. Profiles: Azure CDN Standard from Microsoft (rules engine), Verizon (advanced HTTP), Akamai (real-time stats). Azure Front Door (AFD) is a modern cloud CDN with: global HTTP load balancing, TLS termination, web application firewall (WAF), URL rewrite/redirect, path-based routing, latency-based routing, caching acceleration. Front Door operates at layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS). WAF policies protect against SQL injection, XSS, bots, DDoS. Private link support for origin access.

# Create Front Door profile
az afd profile create \
  --profile-name my-afd \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --sku Premium_AzureFrontDoor

# Create endpoint
az afd endpoint create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --profile-name my-afd \
  --endpoint-name my-app \
  --enabled-state Enabled

# Add origin group
az afd origin-group create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --profile-name my-afd \
  --origin-group-name app-servers \
  --probe-request-type GET \
  --probe-protocol Http \
  --probe-interval-in-seconds 30

# Add route
az afd route create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --profile-name my-afd \
  --endpoint-name my-app \
  --forwarding-protocol MatchRequest \
  --link-to-default-domain Enabled \
  --origin-group app-servers \
  --supported-protocols Http Https \
  --patterns "/*"

Azure Virtual Network: Azure VNet is your isolated network in Azure. Address space defined by CIDR. Subnets segment the VNet; each subnet can have a Network Security Group (NSG) with allow/deny rules. Azure Bastion provides RDP/SSH without public IPs. Service Endpoints connect PaaS services privately via Microsoft backbone. Private Link exposes services privately from your VNet (like your own service behind a private IP). VNet Peering connects VNets within same region (low latency). Global VNet Peering connects across regions. VPN Gateway connects on-premises via IPsec. ExpressRoute is dedicated private connection to Azure.

# Create VNet
az network vnet create \
  --name my-vnet \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name web-subnet \
  --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24

# Create additional subnet
az network vnet subnet create \
  --vnet-name my-vnet \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --name data-subnet \
  --address-prefix 10.0.2.0/24

# NSG with rules
az network nsg create --name web-nsg --resource-group my-rg
az network nsg rule create --nsg-name web-nsg --resource-group my-rg --name AllowHTTPS \
  --priority 100 --destination-port-ranges 443 --protocol Tcp --access Allow

# VNet Peering
az network vnet peering create --name peer1 --resource-group my-rg --vnet-name my-vnet --remote-vnet vnet-yyy --allow-vnet-access

# Private Link (for PaaS)
az network private-link-service create --name my-pls --resource-group my-rg --vnet-name my-vnet --subnet data-subnet
Azure Load Balancer & Traffic Manager: Azure Load Balancer (L4): distributes TCP/UDP traffic across VMs. SKUs: Basic (no HA, no SLA) and Standard (99.99% SLA, availability zones, HA ports, outbound rules). Inbound NAT rules for direct VM access. Backend pools: VMs, VMSS, IP addresses. Health probes check endpoint health. Azure Application Gateway (L7): HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with WAF, URL-based routing, SSL termination, session affinity, rewrite rules. Traffic Manager: DNS-based traffic routing (performance, geographic, priority, weighted, multi-value). Azure DNS hosts domains.

# Create Standard Load Balancer
az network lb create \
  --name my-lb \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --sku Standard \
  --frontend-ip-name my-frontend \
  --backend-pool-name my-backend \
  --public-ip-address my-pip

# Health probe
az network lb probe create --lb-name my-lb --resource-group my-rg --name http-probe --protocol Tcp --port 80

# Load balancing rule
az network lb rule create --lb-name my-lb --resource-group my-rg --name http-rule \
  --protocol Tcp --frontend-port 80 --backend-port 80 \
  --frontend-ip-name my-frontend --backend-pool-name my-backend \
  --probe-name http-probe

# Application Gateway (L7)
az network application-gateway create --name my-appgw --resource-group my-rg --sku WAF_v2 \
  --capacity 2 --vnet-name my-vnet --subnet appgw-subnet \
  --frontend-port 443 --http-settings-port 80 --http-settings-protocol Http \
  --public-ip-address my-pip

# Traffic Manager
az network traffic-manager profile create --name my-tm --resource-group my-rg --routing-method Performance
Azure DNS & Private DNS: Azure DNS hosts domains and provides name resolution. Authoritative DNS — no need to buy a separate DNS provider. Alias records map to Azure resources (free, zone apex support). Private DNS zones resolve names within VNets without public DNS. Auto-registration of VMs in Private DNS. Conditional forwarding for hybrid networks. Azure DDoS Protection (Basic: free, automatic; Standard: $3k/mo, advanced mitigation, analytics, DRT). Network Watcher monitors and diagnoses network issues (topology, IP flow verify, next hop, packet capture, VPN troubleshoot, connection monitor).

# Create DNS zone
az network dns zone create --resource-group my-rg --name example.com

# Create record
az network dns record-set a add-record \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --zone-name example.com \
  --record-set-name www \
  --ipv4-address 203.0.113.10

# Alias record (points to Azure resource)
az network dns record-set a create --resource-group my-rg --zone-name example.com --name api --target-resource /subscriptions/.../frontdoors/my-afd

# Private DNS zone
az network private-dns zone create --resource-group my-rg --name internal.contoso.com
az network private-dns link vnet create --zone-name internal.contoso.com --name my-link --virtual-network my-vnet --registration-enabled true

# Network Watcher (flow logs)
az network watcher flow-log create --nsg web-nsg --resource-group my-rg --workspace my-workspace --traffic-analytics true
Azure Security Center & Defender: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Azure Security Center + Defender for Cloud) provides unified security management. Defender plans: Defender for Servers, Databases, Storage, Containers, Key Vault, App Service, SQL, DNS, Resource Manager. Key Vault stores secrets, keys, and certificates with HSM option. Access policies vs RBAC. Soft delete and purge protection. Azure Policy for compliance (SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001). Sentinel is cloud-native SIEM (Microsoft's Splunk alternative). Secure Score measures security posture. Just-in-Time (JIT) VM access for temporary admin.

# Key Vault
az keyvault create --name my-kv --resource-group my-rg --location eastus --sku Standard

# Store secret
az keyvault secret set --vault-name my-kv --name db-password --value "P@ssw0rd!"

# Grant VM access via managed identity
az keyvault set-policy --name my-kv --object-id $(az vm show --name my-vm --resource-group my-rg --query identity.principalId -o tsv) --secret-permissions get list

# Enable Defender for Cloud (via Portal)
# - Go to Microsoft Defender for Cloud
# - Enable Defender plans
# - Configure email notifications
# - Review Secure Score

# Just-in-Time VM access
az security jit-policy create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --vm-name my-vm \
  --port 22 --protocol Tcp --max-request-access-duration 3h --allowed-source-address-prefixes "203.0.113.0/24"

Azure Account & Portal: Create an Azure account at portal.azure.com. Free tier: $200 credit for 30 days + 55+ always-free services. Azure Portal is the web UI. Azure CLI for command-line management. PowerShell Az module for scripting. Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is the deployment and management layer. Every resource belongs to a resource group. Subscriptions group resource groups with billing boundaries. Management groups organize subscriptions hierarchically. Azure Blueprints for compliance.

# Install Azure CLI
# curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | bash

az login

# List subscriptions
az account list --output table

# Set active subscription
az account set --subscription "MySubscription"

# Create resource group
az group create --name my-rg --location eastus

# List regions
az account list-locations --output table
Azure Regions & Availability: Azure has 60+ regions worldwide, more than any other cloud provider. Region pairs (e.g., East US + West US) are 300+ miles apart for DR. Availability Sets (up to 3 fault domains + 5 update domains) for VMs. Availability Zones (3+ per region) are physically separate data centers within a region. Azure Site Recovery replicates workloads to a secondary region for disaster recovery. Proximity Placement Groups reduce VM-to-VM latency.

# List VMs by region
az vm list-sizes --location eastus --output table

# Check if region supports availability zones
az vm list-availability-zones --location eastus

# Region pairs:
# East US <-> West US
# UK South <-> UK West
# Southeast Asia <-> East Asia
# North Europe <-> West Europe
Azure Resource Manager & RBAC: ARM manages all resources via declarative JSON/Bicep templates. Every resource has a unique ARM ID. RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): roles are assignments of permissions at a scope (subscription, resource group, resource). Built-in roles: Owner, Contributor, Reader, User Access Administrator. Custom roles define granular permissions. Managed Identities give Azure resources an identity in Entra ID without managing credentials. Azure Policy enforces rules across resources.

# ARM resource ID format
# /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/{provider}/{type}/{name}

# RBAC role assignment
az role assignment create \
  --assignee user@example.com \
  --role Reader \
  --resource-group my-rg

# Create custom role
az role definition create --role-definition '{
  "Name": "VM Operator",
  "Description": "Can start/stop VMs",
  "Actions": [
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action",
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/deallocate/action"
  ],
  "AssignableScopes": ["/subscriptions/xxx"]
}'

# Azure Policy: enforce tag
az policy assignment create --policy "require-tag" --parameters '{"tagName":{"value":"Environment"}}'
Azure Entra ID (formerly Active Director: Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud identity service. Previously Azure AD. Tenants represent organizations. Users and Groups manage access. App registrations for OAuth2/OIDC authentication. Service principals are identities for applications. Managed identities for Azure resources (system-assigned or user-assigned). Conditional Access policies enforce MFA, device compliance, location. Privileged Identity Management (PIM) provides just-in-time admin access. Identity Protection detects compromised credentials.

# List users
az ad user list --output table

# Create group
az ad group create --display-name "Developers" --mail-nickname developers

# Add member
az ad group member add --group Developers --member-id xxx

# Create app registration
az ad app create --display-name "my-app"

# Managed identity for VM
az vm identity assign --resource-group my-rg --vm-name my-vm

# Conditional Access (via Portal or Graph API)
# Requires Microsoft Graph - not available via Azure CLI

Azure SQL Database: Azure SQL Database is fully managed SQL Server (PaaS). Service tiers: General Purpose (serverless or provisioned, 5-99.99% HA), Business Critical (always-on, 99.995% HA), Hyperscale (up to 100TB, fast scaling). Elastic Pools share resources among multiple databases (cost-effective for many DBs with spiky usage). Geo-replication for DR (readable secondaries in other regions). Auto-failover groups for transparent failover. Azure SQL Managed Instance (SQL MI) is near-100% SQL Server compatible, with full network isolation. Advanced data security: vulnerability assessment, data discovery, threat detection.

# Create SQL Database server
az sql server create \
  --name my-sql-server \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --admin-user admin \
  --admin-password P@ssw0rd!

# Create database
az sql db create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --server my-sql-server \
  --name my-db \
  --service-objective GP_Gen5_2

# Elastic pool
az sql elastic-pool create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --server my-sql-server \
  --name my-pool \
  --edition GeneralPurpose \
  --capacity 4 --max-capacity 16

# Add DB to pool
az sql db create --resource-group my-rg --server my-sql-server --name db2 --elastic-pool my-pool

# Geo-replication
az sql db replica create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --server my-sql-server \
  --name my-db \
  --partner-server my-secondary-server --partner-resource-group my-rg
Azure Database for MySQL & PostgreSQL: Flexible Server (recommended) vs Single Server (legacy). Flexible Server features: zone-redundant HA, stop/start, burstable SKUs, private networking (VNet), up to 16TB storage, 35-day backup retention. Read replicas (up to 10). Azure Database for PostgreSQL: supports PostgreSQL 16+, pg_cron, pg_hint_plan, PostGIS, and other extensions. Built-in connection pooling with PgBouncer. Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL (formerly Hyperscale, Citus) distributes data across shards for multi-tenant apps. Azure Database Migration Service simplifies migration from on-prem.

# Create PostgreSQL Flexible Server
az postgres flexible-server create \
  --name my-pg-server \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --admin-user admin \
  --admin-password P@ssw0rd! \
  --sku-name Standard_D2s_v3 \
  --tier GeneralPurpose \
  --version 16 \
  --high-availability ZoneRedundancy \
  --storage-size 128

# Create MySQL Flexible Server
az mysql flexible-server create \
  --name my-mysql-server \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --admin-user admin \
  --admin-password P@ssw0rd! \
  --version 8.0 \
  --tier Burstable \
  --sku-name Standard_B1ms

# Create read replica
az postgres flexible-server replica create \
  --replica-name my-replica \
  --source-name my-pg-server \
  --resource-group my-rg
Azure Cosmos DB: Cosmos DB is globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database. APIs: NoSQL (native document), MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Cassandra, Gremlin (graph), Table (key-value). Single-digit ms latency at any scale. Multi-region writes (active-active) for 99.999% availability. Automatic and instant scaling (RU/s — Request Units per second). Analytical store for HTAP (hybrid transactional/analytical processing). Change Feed triggers Azure Functions. Point-in-time backup (continuous backup mode). Dedicated gateway for query routing. SLA-backed 99.999% read availability globally.

# Create Cosmos DB account
az cosmosdb create \
  --name my-cosmos \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --kind GlobalDocumentDB \
  --locations regionName=eastus failoverPriority=0 \
  --locations regionName=westus failoverPriority=1 \
  --enable-multiple-write-locations true \
  --default-consistency-level Session

# Create database and container
az cosmosdb sql database create --account-name my-cosmos --resource-group my-rg --name my-db
az cosmosdb sql container create \
  --account-name my-cosmos \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --database-name my-db \
  --name users \
  --partition-key-path "/userId" \
  --throughput 1000

# Query (NoSQL API)
# SELECT * FROM users u WHERE u.city = 'NYC'
# SELECT u.id, u.name FROM users u ORDER BY u.createdAt OFFSET 10 LIMIT 20
Azure Cache for Redis: Azure Cache for Redis is managed Redis. Tiers: Basic (single node, dev/test, no SLA), Standard (replicated, 99.9% SLA), Premium (persistence, clustering, VNet, 99.95% SLA), Enterprise (Redis Enterprise, active geo-replication, modules: RediSearch, RedisJSON, RedisTimeSeries, RedisBloom), Enterprise Flash (tiered storage, lower cost). Redis Cluster splits data across shards. Persistence: RDB (snapshots) or AOF (write-ahead log). Data eviction policies (LRU, TTL, LFU, random). Geo-replication for DR. Private endpoint for secure access.

# Create Redis cache
az redis create \
  --name my-redis \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Premium \
  --vm-size P1 \
  --enable-non-ssl-port \
  --minimum-tls-version 1.2

# Get connection string
az redis show --name my-redis --resource-group my-rg --query "hostName"

# Connect via redis-cli
# redis-cli -h my-redis.redis.cache.windows.net -p 6380 -a AccessKey --tls

# Enterprise (RediSearch)
# FT.CREATE idx ON HASH PREFIX 1 "product:" SCHEMA name TEXT price NUMERIC
# FT.SEARCH idx "@name:laptop*" SORTBY price DESC LIMIT 0 10

ARM & Bicep: ARM templates (JSON) and Bicep (DSL, compiles to ARM) are Azure's IaC. Bicep is simpler: concise syntax, module support, intellisense, idempotent deployments. Resources reference each other via symbolic names. Modules decompose infrastructure into reusable files. Parameters, variables, outputs. Conditions and loops for conditional/count-based resources. Deployment scopes: resource group, subscription, management group. What-If shows changes before applying. Deployment stacks manage groups of resources as a single unit.

# Bicep template (main.bicep)
param location string = resourceGroup().location
param envName string = 'production'

var uniqueName = 'app-${uniqueString(resourceGroup().id)}'

resource storage 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts@2023-01-01' = {
  name: uniqueName
  location: location
  kind: 'StorageV2'
  sku: { name: 'Standard_GRS' }
  tags: { Environment: envName }
}

output storageEndpoint string = storage.properties.primaryEndpoints.blob

# Deploy
az deployment group create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --template-file main.bicep \
  --parameters envName=staging

# What-If (preview changes)
az deployment group what-if --resource-group my-rg --template-file main.bicep

# Module (storage.bicep)
# resource stg ...
# output endpoint string = stg.properties.primaryEndpoints.blob
# 
# main.bicep: module stg 'storage.bicep' = { name: 'storageDeploy' }
Azure DevOps Pipelines: Azure DevOps provides CI/CD with Pipelines (build/test/deploy), Repos (Git), Boards (work tracking), Test Plans, Artifacts (package feeds). YAML pipelines define stages (sequential), jobs (parallel per stage), steps (tasks). Multi-stage: Build → Test → Deploy to staging → Approve → Deploy to production. Environments track deployments with approvals and checks. Service connections to Azure, GitHub, Docker, etc. Self-hosted agents run in your network. Variable groups and library for secrets. Integration with GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab.

# azure-pipelines.yml
trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main]

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: BuildJob
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '20.x'
    - script: |
        npm install
        npm run build
      displayName: 'Build app'
    - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
      inputs:
        PathtoPublish: 'dist'
        ArtifactName: 'drop'

- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployToWeb
    environment: 'production'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureWebApp@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'my-connection'
              appName: 'my-app'
              package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/**/*.zip'
Azure Monitor: Azure Monitor collects and analyzes telemetry from Azure resources. Log Analytics workspaces store logs and metrics. Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries logs (like SQL for logs). Application Insights monitors live web apps (request rates, response times, failure rates, dependency tracking, distributed tracing, user behavior analytics). Smart detection highlights anomalies. Metrics Explorer visualizes numeric data. Alerts: metric, log, activity log, smart groups. Action groups send email, SMS, webhook, ITSM. Workbooks are interactive reports (parameterized, multi-visualization). Managed Grafana for dashboards.

# Create Log Analytics workspace
az monitor log-analytics workspace create \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --workspace-name my-logs

# Application Insights
az monitor app-insights component create \
  --app my-app \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --kind web

Azure Automation & Logic Apps: Azure Automation automates repetitive tasks: VM start/stop, patch management, configuration management. Runbooks (PowerShell, Python) execute on schedule or via webhook. Update Management assesses and installs OS updates. Change Tracking detects configuration changes. Desired State Configuration (DSC) enforces VM config state. Logic Apps are serverless workflows (visual designer, 400+ connectors). Triggers: HTTP, schedule, Azure services. Actions: condition, switch, parallel branches, loops. Enterprise integration: AS2, EDIFACT, X12, RosettaNet.

Azure DevOps: Azure DevOps provides CI/CD with Pipelines (build/test/deploy), Repos (Git), Boards (work tracking), Test Plans, Artifacts (package feeds). YAML pipelines define stages (sequential), jobs (parallel per stage), steps (tasks). Multi-stage: Build to Test to Deploy with manual approval gates. Environments track deployments with approvals and checks. Service connections to Azure, GitHub, Docker. Self-hosted agents run in your network for custom dependencies. Variable groups and library for secrets. Common mistake: hardcoding secrets in pipelines — use Azure Key Vault integration or variable group secrets.

# azure-pipelines.yml (multi-stage)
trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main]

variables:
  - group: production-vars
  - name: buildConfig
    value: Release

stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: BuildJob
    steps:
    - task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
      inputs:
        command: build
        arguments: --configuration $(buildConfig)
    - task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
      inputs:
        command: test
    - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
      inputs:
        PathtoPublish: '$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)'
        ArtifactName: 'drop'

- stage: DeployStaging
  dependsOn: Build
  condition: succeeded()
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployToStaging
    environment: staging
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureWebApp@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'my-connection'
              appName: 'my-app-staging'
              package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/**/*.zip'

- stage: DeployProduction
  dependsOn: DeployStaging
  condition: succeeded()
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployToProduction
    environment: production
    strategy:
      rolling:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureWebApp@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'my-connection'
              appName: 'my-app'
              package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/**/*.zip'
Azure Key Vault: Key Vault stores secrets, encryption keys, and certificates. Soft delete (enabled by default) retains deleted items for retention period (90 days default). Purge protection prevents permanent deletion. Managed Identities (system-assigned or user-assigned) let Azure resources (VMs, App Services, Functions) authenticate to Key Vault without credentials. RBAC for Key Vault uses Azure RBAC (data plane) — preferred over access policies for modern setups. Key Vault Firewall restricts access by IP and VNet. Key rotation can be automated with Event Grid + Functions. Common mistake: storing secrets in code or config files instead of Key Vault. Enable diagnostics logs to audit secret access.

# Create Key Vault with RBAC authorization
az keyvault create --name my-kv --resource-group my-rg --location eastus --sku Standard --enable-rbac-authorization

# Assign role (grant VM access to secrets)
az role assignment create \
  --assignee $(az vm show --name my-vm --resource-group my-rg --query identity.principalId -o tsv) \
  --role "Key Vault Secrets User" \
  --scope /subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/my-kv

# Store and retrieve a secret
az keyvault secret set --vault-name my-kv --name db-password --value "P@ssw0rd!"
az keyvault secret show --vault-name my-kv --name db-password

# Create and import a key
az keyvault key create --vault-name my-kv --name my-rsa-key --protection software
# az keyvault key import --vault-name my-kv --name my-key --byok-file ./key.pem

# Certificate operations
az keyvault certificate create --vault-name my-kv --name my-cert --policy @policy.json

# Enable soft delete and purge protection
az keyvault update --name my-kv --enable-soft-delete true --enable-purge-protection true

# Diagnostics (send logs to workspace)
az monitor diagnostic-settings create --resource my-kv --workspace my-logs --metrics '[{"category": "AllMetrics", "enabled": true}]'
Azure Logic Apps: Logic Apps are serverless workflows with a visual designer and 400+ connectors. Triggers: HTTP request, schedule (recurrence), Azure services (Blob created, Event Grid), SaaS (Salesforce, Slack). Actions: condition, switch, parallel branches, loops (forEach, until), compose/parse JSON. Managed connectors: Office 365, SharePoint, Dynamics 365, Service Bus, SQL Server. Integration Account for enterprise B2B (AS2, EDIFACT, X12, RosettaNet). Built-in connectors run natively for higher performance. Common mistake: not handling transient failures — configure retry policies on actions. Consumption plan (pay per action) vs Standard plan (dedicated, better performance, VNet integration).
Azure Event Grid: Event Grid is a fully managed event routing service. Events are JSON payloads describing what happened. Topics: system topics (Azure service events like Blob Created, VM Deleted) and custom topics (your own events). Subscriptions: push to Event Handlers (Functions, Webhooks, Service Bus, Queue Storage, Hybrid Connections, Logic Apps). Event filtering by event type, subject prefix/suffix, or advanced filters (numeric ranges, boolean, string contains). Retry policy: exponential backoff (up to 30 days). Dead-letter destination for failed events. Common mistake: forgetting to validate webhook endpoints (Event Grid requires endpoint validation handshake). Up to 10M events/sec per region.

# Create custom topic
az eventgrid topic create --name my-topic --resource-group my-rg --location eastus

# Create subscription (Event Hub endpoint)
az eventgrid event-subscription create \
  --name my-sub \
  --source-resource-id /subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/topics/my-topic \
  --endpoint-type eventhub \
  --endpoint /subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.EventHub/namespaces/my-eh/eventhubs/my-hub

# Create subscription with advanced filtering
az eventgrid event-subscription create \
  --name filtered-sub \
  --source-resource-id /subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/topics/my-topic \
  --endpoint-type webhook \
  --endpoint https://my-app.azurewebsites.net/api/events \
  --advanced-filter data.orderStatus stringin shipped delivered \
  --advanced-filter data.total numberinrange 100 10000 \
  --deadletter-endpoint /subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/my-storage/blobServices/default/containers/deadletter

# Publish custom event
az eventgrid event-subscription create --name my-sub --source-resource-id /subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/topics/my-topic \
  --endpoint https://my-app.azurewebsites.net/api/events

# Publish event (using curl)
# curl -X POST https://my-topic.eastus-1.eventgrid.azure.net/api/events \
#   -H "aeg-sas-key: xxx" \
#   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
#   -d '[{"id": "1", "eventType": "order.created", "subject": "orders/123", "data": {"orderId": "123", "total": 99.99}, "dataVersion": "1.0"}]'

# Webhook endpoint validation (must respond)
# Return validation code in response body: {"validationResponse": "<code>"}
API Management: API Management (APIM) publishes APIs to external and internal consumers. Products group APIs with access rules and rate limits. Subscriptions: product access keys for developers. Policies: XML-based transformation, validation, rate limiting, CORS, caching, IP filtering, JWT validation. Policy scopes: global, product, API, operation. Versioning: URL-based or header-based version schemes. Multiple deployment regions for low latency. Self-hosted gateway for on-prem/hybrid. Developer portal for API documentation and testing. Common mistake: exposing backend implementation details — use policies to transform requests/responses. Enable diagnostic logging for monitoring API usage and errors.

# Create APIM instance
az apim create --name my-apim --resource-group my-rg --location eastus --publisher-name MyCompany --publisher-email admin@company.com --sku-name Developer

# Import API from OpenAPI/Swagger
az apim api import --resource-group my-rg --service-name my-apim \
  --path /api --api-id my-api \
  --specification-format OpenApi --specification-url https://my-app.azurewebsites.net/swagger/v1/swagger.json

# Create product
az apim product create --resource-group my-rg --service-name my-apim \
  --product-id gold-tier --product-name "Gold Tier" --description "Premium API access" \
  --subscription-required true --approval-required true --subscriptions-limit 5 --state published

# Add API to product
az apim product api add --resource-group my-rg --service-name my-apim --product-id gold-tier --api-id my-api

#   <backend>
#     <base />

#   </outbound>
